page0.text:
This is clearly a trap.
I'm curious about what Zouken has to say, but I can't leave Sakura right now.

page1.text:
"I refuse. I don't trust you. Tell him to come here if he wants to talk."
"I see. Then I shall relay your message."

page2.text:
That's all Assassin says before he disappears.
He's probably on the way back to Zouken by now.

page3.text:
"...Good. I made the right choice."
Even if I got to meet Zouken alone, I have no way to defeat him.
And he's a monster that can't be reasoned with.
I shouldn't face Zouken until we have all of our weapons at the ready.

page4.text:
"...The Jeweled Sword, huh."
It's the name of the trump card that Tohsaka and Illya are trying to make.
Archer's arm contains records of a thousand or more famous, magical swords, but this isn't among them.

page5.text:
"...But we can win if I replicate this. I can believe in that, right, Tohsaka?"
I rest my heavy body on the ground.
...I'm a little tired. I should sleep.
Once I wake up, I can check on Sakura, make some food, and help Tohsaka and Illya with their work...

page6.text:
"Mm...mm."
I awaken to the presence of dinner.
Dinner has a "presence", of course. It's the sound of a chef knife on a cutting board, the low chatter of the TV, and the smell of delicious food in the making.

page7.text:
"...Huh?"
I find Sakura's pajamas, an empty bowl, and a wet towel in the room.

page8.text:
...
I search my memory.
Based on the situation, I checked on Sakura sometime in the afternoon.
I try to recall the details, but stop.
That doesn't matter now.
It just slipped my mind, so it isn't worth thinking about now.

page9.text:
Tohsaka must be making dinner.
Sakura and Illya aren't here.
Sakura must be in her bedroom, while Illya's in the tatami room.

page10.text:
"Huh? You're back? You said you were going to take a break since you're tired."
...
My face stiffens for an instant.
"Nah, I'll help. You must be tired, too. Sorry for dumping it all on you."
I respond as naturally as I can to avoid suspicion.

page11.text:
"Dummy. I appreciate the thought, but you can't even hold a knife with that arm. I've got tonight, so go and rest."
I hear the satisfying sound of knife on cutting board.
Tohsaka's finely slicing a lot of bell peppers. Maybe we're having vegetable stir-fry tonight.

page12.text:
"...Oh, I should get ready to take a bath. I'll take care of the laundry too, so can I take in your clothes?"
"O-of course not, you idiot! I'll do that myself!"
The sound of the knife becomes fierce and gallant.
Tohsaka's cutting beef into chunks. Maybe we're having beef for dinner.

page13.text:
"I wonder which it is."
I grumble as I start to make my way to the bathroom.
Whatever we're having, I'm looking forward to the final—

page14.text:
"Eh...?"
The lights go out on their own.
"Is it a power outage...?"

page15.text:
"...Looks like it. I didn't touch the light switch."
"...Yeah. There was no response from the Bounded Field, so it can't be an intruder."
"Yeah. Even if Zouken attacks, we'd at least hear an alarm—"

page16.text:
No, we wouldn't.
Remember what happened this morning.
Assassin might be able to breach the Emiya house's Bounded Field without setting it off!

page17.text:
"Stay here, Tohsaka. I'm going to check on things, just in case."
"Huh...? Hold on, I should go too. It's dangerous on your own."

page18.text:
"Oh, right... No, you should go to Sakura. I'll join you once I get Illya."
"Okay. I got Sakura."

page19.text:
I go to Illya's tatami room.
It's quiet, but the house feels the way it always does.
"Maybe I'm overthinking it. It's just a blackout."
Still, I should wake Illya up while I'm at it.
Even if the power's out, it's almost time for dinner.

page20.text:
"Illya, are you awake?"
I slide open the door.
...
I'm greeted by a vicious mural of bloodstains.

page21.text:
"Illya..."
Illya isn't here.
All I see in the room is blood.
I think I see something that looks like a bundle of silver thread in the corner of the blood-drenched room, but that isn't Illya.
It's not Illya anymore.

page22.text:
I run out of the room.
My mind has gone stone cold, and I head for the guestrooms.
Sakura's in danger.
I grasp the situation in a second without really understanding anything at all, and take the shortest path through the backyard.

page23.text:
There...
I see something that shouldn't exist.

page24.text:
"...Oh."
It's like the story about that ghost under a willow tree.
Why didn't the Bounded Field react?
What is this thing doing here?
Before I even process my own question,
I lose any chance to flee, any avenue of escape.
Shadows already cover the entire house.
It's made of shadow, so there's no getting away from it in the lightless night.

page25.text:
I learned that last night.
The second I run into this thing, my life is over.

page26.text:
The ribbon-like tentacles impale me through the chest like a crowbar.
It easily tears me open,
like a blooming red flower.
This must be how Illya stopped being Illya.
